equation: dX = mu1 * X * dt + sigma1 * X * dW1;  dY = mu2 * Y * dt + sigma2 * Y * dW2;  corr(dW1, dW2) = rho
diffusion_derivative: N/A for multi-D (Milstein requires Levy area for cross terms)
implementation_notes: 2D correlated GBM with near-singular correlation rho=0.95 and elevated volatility sigma=0.30. Introduce correlation via Cholesky on the increments: dW1 = sqrt(dt)*Z1, dW_corr = rho*Z1 + sqrt(1-rho**2)*Z2 (times sqrt(dt)). X and Y are stepped independently after generating the correlated increments. Use EM only (multi-D Milstein needs Levy areas). Per-component marginals are exact GBM, so the analytic moments are the standard GBM moments per component and are unaffected by rho. High rho makes the Cholesky factor ill-conditioned but does not change the marginal moments; the elevated volatility widens the terminal lognormal distribution, so 50000 paths are needed to hit the 10% variance tolerance.
